output.brief: Don't roll back the gateway. The latency jump comes from the storage compaction tuning change pushed fleet-wide on the evening of 2 Nov, not from gateway 5.8. In every cell that received the push, latency rose within minutes, even in cells still running gateway 5.7. One cell (aps-3) skipped the push but did get 5.8, and its latency stayed at about 94 ms. Rolling euw-1 back to 5.7 changed nothing. Storage-node data fits: compaction took 71% of disk bytes, disks hit 97% utilisation, and node-side GET time went from 61 to 262 ms. The network shows no fault. Traffic growth was small. A rollback would cost about 4 hours, leave the problem in place, and reopen the signature security hole. Next step: revert the tuning in one cell first and watch GET p99 and compaction backlog, then extend the revert if both behave. Backlog is about 11% against a 15% danger line, so watch it closely. Don't pause compaction entirely. Rate-limiting Orrin is an optional backstop; the source of backlog growth is still unattributed until the 10 Nov report. I'm fairly confident, about 85%.
